perspective:
Angela’s accessible information:

- She knows she is Angela Hwang, a hairdresser with a doctorate. She knows Kevin Flores as a close friend since high school, a construction worker, and someone she confides in.
- In their coffee conversation, she invited Kevin because she was worried he seemed unhappy with his job. She heard Kevin say he was “alright, just the usual grind,” then admit he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was going through the motions. She asked if he had considered another job or career path. Kevin said he had thought about it but did not know where to start and felt overwhelmed. She offered to explore options together; Kevin agreed and thanked her.
- She found job openings and a career-counseling service and shared them with Kevin. Kevin told her he had been thinking a lot and was interested in something creative, maybe design or architecture. She encouraged him, said he would be great at that, and suggested he check the resources. Kevin said he would and thanked her.
- She believed Kevin was hesitant and felt frustrated/worried. She arranged a meeting with a career coach and told Kevin. Kevin said she did not have to, appreciated it, but was not sure he was ready. She said she understood his hesitation but thought a push could help and that the coach could help him plan and gain confidence. Kevin agreed to give it a shot. She promised to support him.
- She checked in about the career coach. Kevin told her the coach was helpful, he had started online design courses, and he felt more confident about the change. She said she was proud and offered more help. Kevin said her support was enough and he would ask if he needed anything. She reaffirmed she would always be there.
- She believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career. She organized a small celebration party and told him. Kevin thanked her. She said he had worked hard and come far and it was time to celebrate. Kevin said he was grateful and could not have done it without her. She said he did the hard work and invited him to enjoy the party. Kevin agreed.
- Her own feelings/beliefs across these events: concerned for Kevin, supportive and hopeful, frustrated/worried when he seemed hesitant, proud/relieved as he progressed, and happy/satisfied when celebrating.

She does not have access to Kevin’s private thoughts beyond what he told her, nor to narrator-only labels such as his personality type unless she otherwise learned them.
